text.tspan: Along the upper Min River, who counted as “one of us” depended on which village you asked.
Upper Min River valley · a schematic field scene
Draw a circle. Its rim tells you where
it ends. To study a people, Wang asks
where people themselves draw the line.
Neighbours may speak alike and use
the same tools, yet call themselves by
different names. Who counts as kin?
Sharing a spring can draw households
together. A claim to pasture can set
A hero can stand at the head of a line
villages a way to speak of kinship.
Walk upstream. The village that one
settlement calls an outsider may call
the next village an outsider in turn.
Some forebears recur in every telling.
Others fade as ties change. Wang calls
In one valley account, three brothers founded three villages. A story told across four valleys
could begin with four brothers. The remembered family grew with the circle of neighbours.
Source: Wang Ming-ke, Huaxia Frontier, 2020 Chinese edition, prefatory essay, pp. 10–11, and Part I.
